rationale: M60-C (#921). A `contains` edge carried the child symbol's `range.startLine` — the line the whole DECLARATION starts on — with the comment that 'the edge moves WITH its symbol, so edge and symbol range can never disagree'. That is right until the declaration's start and its NAME are different lines, which is exactly the shape the M59 Tier A oracle found 166 times on its 120-file c/cpp sample (101 in the c lane, 65 in cpp): `void NORETURN` then `CheckFailed(const char *file, …)`, `typedef StackDepotBase<…>` then `StackDepot;`, `static TwoLevelMap<…>` then `useCounts;`, `struct { … } options;` (name on the closing line), `extern "C" int __attribute__((weak))` then the function name. Every other relationship type already follows the name-on-line rule (`nameLine` prefers the grammar's `name` field), and the M59 oracle checks exactly that rule, so the containment edge was the only kind that could disagree with it. The fix keeps the symbol's RANGE on the whole declaration node (search, edit anchors and the M73 line base read that) and moves the EDGE's line to the name: `meta.nameLine`, recorded where the name node is in hand. This fixture is the smallest file that can tell the two readings apart: a wrapped free function, a wrapped member, an anonymous aggregate member whose name is on the closing line, and a wrapped class-scope typedef — plus same-line controls (`Widget`, `take`, the nested aggregate member `bits`) whose two candidate lines coincide, so a rule that drifted on ordinary declarations would fail here too. Lines 14/22/26/31 are the declaration starts and are forbidden because the names are on 15/23/28/32. NOTE ON SCOPE: the c lane's own analyzer ranges a struct/union MEMBER at its declarator (`rawDecl` skips the type specifiers), so in C the two lines already coincide — measured on the c fixture beside this one; the 101 'c lane' rows the oracle reported were produced by THIS analyzer, on .h files that lane draws and the product dispatches to cpp (language-detection policy).

expectSymbols.name: bits
expectSymbols.note: CORRECTED by ONTOLOGY/D19, and the correction is the point rather than a relaxation. `struct { unsigned bits : 1; } options;` gives the struct NO name — C++ writes none — so the analyzer used to publish the literal string `anonymous` for it and `bits` was owned by that string. An anonymous struct's members are members of the ENCLOSING class ([class.union.anon]), so `Widget` is the correct owner AND a resolvable one: pre-fix this edge resolved to a name 92 distinct scopes share corpus-wide. Measured over the two pinned C++ corpora: 133 `anonymous` symbols and 1,611 relationship rows carrying the sentinel as an endpoint, 20 of them `contains` rows with it as the TARGET. The forbid row below pins the sentinel is ABSENT, which is the half `ownerName` alone cannot state.

expectRelationships.note: `long long` is on 14; the name is written on 15
`unsigned long long` is on 22; the name is written on 23
`struct {` is on 26; the member's name is on the closing line 28
`typedef unsigned long` is on 31; the alias name is written on 32
CONTROL: `class Widget {` — declaration start and name on the same line

CONTROL, and it keeps the control's original purpose: `unsigned bits : 1;` is written entirely on 27, so the declaration's start and the name's line COINCIDE and a rule that drifted on ordinary one-line declarations would fail here. The `from` changed from the sentinel to `Widget` under D19; the line this fixture is about (#921) is unchanged, which is why the pin is on the line and not only on the endpoints.

the body's line is not the name's either — a rule keyed to the first line of the BODY is visible here

PRE-D19: the anonymous aggregate published as a class named by this analyzer's own no-name sentinel, which is not a name any C++ program can contain. This was an EXPECTED row before D19 and is the R7 placeholder-literal endpoint the ontology workstream's definition of done forbids. The aggregate is still reachable, through `contains Widget -> options`.

PRE-D19, from the other side: an edge whose SOURCE is the sentinel. 519 corpus `contains` rows and 882 `calls` rows had it as their source, which is how one name came to stand for 92 unrelated scopes.
